description: The deployment rule every calibrated step applies before it acts automatically (cyber_data_collector/dedup/deployment.py). A calibration that matches the current models, questions and evidence is used only when the precision of the automatic action it licenses is shown, with the stated confidence, to be at least the floor - accounting for how many labelled actions the cut-off rests on. A step that fails the rule is report-only, exactly as with a stale calibration. Changing a value here changes what the pipeline does: review it like code.

rationale.confidence: One-sided 95%: the conventional level, and one-sided because only the risk of the automatic action being worse than the floor matters (a better-than-measured step costs nothing). At 95% one wrong decision in twenty about whether to deploy is the accepted risk; 99% would demand 21 all-correct labelled actions before anything could act.
rationale.precision_floor: The cut-offs are chosen where the labelled precision reaches 0.95, but that point estimate is what an unlucky handful of labels can also produce. The floor is what must be demonstrated, not hoped for: with 95% confidence at least 4 of 5 automatic actions are right. Every action here is logged and reversible through the ledger, so 0.80 is the level at which an error costs a later correction rather than a lost incident; a step whose worst plausible precision is below it acts more wrongly than a reviewer would accept. With all labelled actions correct it needs 14 of them (0.80^14 < 0.05), with one wrong 22, with two wrong 30.
rationale.min_labelled_actions: The binomial bound treats labelled actions as independent draws. They are not quite: several can come from one organisation or one supplier breach. A floor on the count (unweighted and effective) keeps a step from acting on a bound that a few correlated cases reach; 15 is one more than the floor alone implies when every action is correct, so it binds only when weighting shrinks the effective count or when the floor is lowered.
rationale.effective_sample_size: Where a calibration is weighted (stratified samples weighted back to their bands), the bound is also computed from Kish's effective sample size n_eff = (sum w)^2 / sum w^2 of the acted-on labelled items, with the weighted precision as the success rate; the lower of the two bounds decides. Weighting can therefore lower n but never raise it.
rationale.require_heldout_evaluation: The cut-off was chosen on the same labels its precision is quoted on, which flatters it. scripts/evaluate_calibrations.py re-chooses the cut-off on folds of the labels with the step's own selection function and measures precision only on the labels not used to choose it (each label held out exactly once; folds are a hash of the subject id, so the split is deterministic). Its exact lower bound must also clear the floor, and a calibration with no evaluation matching it (same identity and generated time) does not act: the evaluation is free (stored scores only) and is the only out-of-sample measurement.
rationale.heldout_folds: Five folds: every label is held out once, so the pooled held-out count is close to the full count (a single 50/50 split would halve it and fail every small step by construction), while each cut-off is still chosen on 80% of the labels.
rationale.bootstrap: The calibrations' bootstrap out-of-sample figures are reported, not gated. Each replicate scores roughly the 37% of acted items left out of the resample, so its 5th percentile on a cut-off resting on 10-20 items moves in steps of 0.05-0.10 on one item, and it is a weighted resampling summary, not a confidence bound. The held-out folds measure the same choose-then-test optimism with an exact bound and do gate.
